about: D.W. Read, Arthur's little sister, eyes a blank sign hanging on a door in the top panel. In the bottom panel she stands in front of the door, hands on her hips, and the subtitle reads "That sign won't stop me, because I can't read!" Her defiant ignorance makes it a joke about ignoring rules, warnings and instructions, either because you didn't read them or because you've decided they don't apply to you. The sign is blank so you can write any rule on it.
origin: The scene is from the PBS cartoon Arthur, in a late-1990s episode featuring D.W. Fans later blanked the sign so it could be relabeled with any warning.
usage:
There is a single box, positioned on the big sign in the top panel. Write a rule, warning or instruction there, phrased the way a real sign or notice would be: "no pushing to main", "do not feed the ducks", "terms and conditions". The subtitle in the bottom panel already delivers the punchline.

It works best with rules that people routinely ignore: "wet floor", "dry clean only", "read the manual first", "no talking during the exam", "maximum 10 items".
aka: That Sign Can't Stop Me Because I Can't Read
